 FDC Limited (NSE:FDC): What Does the Rs 37.22 Cr Tax Refund… 
 Announcements
 By Mukul Kumar 
 Oct 31, 2026
 FDC Limited (NSE:FDC): What Does the Rs 37.22 Cr Tax Refund Mean?
 FDC
 Source: Krish Capital Pty Ltd
 You are reading a free article with opinions that may differ from the recommendation given by Kalkine in its paid research reports. Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More 
 FDC Limited (NSE:FDC) disclosed on 31 October 2026, under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, that it has received income tax refund orders from the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 1(3)(1), Mumbai, determining an aggregate refund of Rs 37.22 crore for Assessment Years 2012-13 and 2014-15.
 Key Highlights
 The Commissioner of Income Tax Appeals (CIT(A)) passed favourable orders dated 29 September 2026, accepting FDC's submissions for AY 2014-15 and AY 2012-13.
 The jurisdictional Assessing Officer subsequently passed effect orders dated 6 October 2026 and 29 October 2026, received by the company on 30 and 31 October 2026 respectively.
 The aggregate refund determined across both assessment years stands at Rs 37.22 crore, inclusive of applicable interest income.
 Interest income forming part of the refund will be credited to the Statement of Profit and Loss as income, per the company's disclosure.
 About the Company
 FDC Limited (NSE:FDC) , headquartered in Mumbai, is a pharmaceutical manufacturer engaged in formulations and active pharmaceutical ingredients across therapeutic segments including ophthalmic, oral rehydration salts, and anti-infectives. The company operates manufacturing facilities across India and markets its products domestically and in select international markets. It is listed on both BSE (scrip code 531599) and NSE.
 Announcement in Detail
 FDC Limited filed the disclosure under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and in accordance with SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/0155 dated 11 November 2024. The appeals before the CIT(A)-56 were filed by the company against disallowances made by the Assessing Officer on account of publicity expenses and deductions claimed under Section 35(2AB) of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
 The CIT(A) accepted the company's submissions and passed favourable orders on 29 September 2026. Following this, the jurisdictional Assessing Officer issued giving-effect orders on 6 October 2026 for AY 2014-15 and on 29 October 2026 for AY 2012-13, together determining a refund of Rs 37.22 crore. The orders were received by FDC on 30 October 2026 and 31 October 2026 respectively.
 Impact on Investors
 The filing shows that the interest component embedded within the Rs 37.22 crore refund will be recognised as income in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the period in which it is received, which investors will note could provide a one-time uplift to reported earnings in the relevant quarter. The disclosed terms indicate this is a concluded administrative process at the giving-effect stage, meaning no further appellate uncertainty exists at the AO or CIT(A) level for these two assessment years.
 Shareholders will observe that the original disputes involved disallowances on publicity expenses and Section 35(2AB) deductions, items common to research-oriented pharmaceutical companies. The resolution removes a contingent liability from these two years, though investors should note that any remaining open assessments for other years are not addressed by this disclosure.
 Sector / Market Context
 India's pharmaceutical industry remains one of the more heavily scrutinised sectors from a transfer pricing and expense-disallowance standpoint, with research-linked deductions under Section 35(2AB) frequently contested by tax authorities. According to FICCI and industry data, Indian pharma companies collectively invest a meaningful share of revenues in research and development, making such deduction disputes a recurring feature of their tax compliance market. Resolutions at the appellate stage, as seen in this case, are a standard outcome of the structured income tax appeals process under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
